Before this file only carving, OPF-feasibility screening (Julia PowerModels AC OPF), datakit generation, label verification and test-id construction ran (no GENCO or interpolator evaluation on them). Mechanics only: none.
question: Candidate 9 found GENCO beats the best learning-free |V| interpolator on all seen-family grids (GOC/EPIGRIDS) but on 8/17 unseen-family grids at 40%. Is that a family-exposure effect? Control: freshly CARVED subgrids of the seen-family parents (grids GENCO has not trained on, from families it was pretrained on), evaluated exactly as candidate 9.

data_construction.carving: datakit has no subgrid/subnetwork procedure (searched gridfm-datakit-repro and the installed gridfm_datakit; the pretraining launcher reads a pre-made directory of subnets_casefiles/*.m). Documented classical alternative (carve.py): parent base point by AC Newton (core/grid_ops/reference_pf, DC start) on the pglib .m, dispatch Pmin+alpha(Pmax-Pmin) covering load+losses; region = seeded BFS from a random root over in-service branches grown to a log-uniform target of 150-950 buses; tie branches removed and their base-point flow folded into the inside boundary bus as extra Pd/Qd, so the region's base point is an exact root of the carved case; REF = largest in-service generator in the region; costs/limits copied from the parent. Rejection: no in-service generator; generation capacity < 1.2 x net load; region load < 20 MW; tie flow sum|dPd| > tie_max x max(region load, region generation) (tier a: tie_max 1.0; tier b: 4.0 used only for parents that produced no tier-a candidate: case4619, 4917, 9591, 10480, 19402); bus-count or branch (r,x) Jaccard >= 0.3 against any of the 31 hosted GENCO training subgrids.
data_construction.screening: every candidate was screened with PowerModels AC OPF (Ipopt); only LOCALLY_SOLVED candidates were kept (tier a: 18 of 30 feasible; tier b: 10 of 16). First two feasible per parent were selected; for the three parents with many feasible candidates (case4837, 30000, 7336) two more were added (round 2). This screening biases toward easier subgrids.
data_construction.generation: genco_challenge.ladder_data (datakit default_pf.yaml with GENCO's evaluation-set edits: one topology variant per load scenario), 120 requested scenarios, collapsed labels dropped by ladder_data.validate_grid.
data_construction.label_verification: verify.py: EVERY generated scenario, power-balance residual max|V conj(Y V) - S| < 1e-6 pu with the scenario's own Ybus, Vm in [0.5,1.5], finite. verified.json. Scenarios failing would be excluded.
data_construction.differences_from_GENCO: OUR CARVING MAY DIFFER FROM GENCO'S (their procedure is not public in the repo): BFS blobs with folded boundary injections vs unknown; our subgrids are smaller (median ~250 buses vs 555 for the 31 hosted ones) and OPF-screened; tier b subgrids are tie-dominated (tie flow 2-4x the internal load/generation); GENCO's subgrids idx 0..50 per parent may overlap our regions physically; only 31 of the 100 training subgrids are available for the leakage fingerprint, the other 69 cannot be checked.
data_construction.leakage: fingerprint vs the 31 hosted training subgrids only (pre-registered rule: same bus count or (r,x) Jaccard >= 0.3 is rejected); max_jaccard per subgrid in the table; 30000_goc has repeated line types so higher Jaccard values reflect type repetition, not shared lines. Disclosed: parent-level exposure is by construction (GENCO trained on other subgrids of these parents).

run_rule: a carved subgrid is in the test iff >= 20 verified test scenarios (graphkit test_ratio 0.99 split intersected with verified labels) and GENCO and all five interpolators produced finite output for every one of them in all 15 configs
conditions: identical to candidate 9 (protocol in ../2026-10-21-genco-voltage-inference-oos/protocol.json): 10/20/40% measured x 3 seeds noise-free; 0.5% noise at 20% and 40% x 3 seeds; methods G, I1-I5 with candidate 9's code (ocommon.py copy, I5 scalable); metric |V| MAE at unmeasured buses vs true |V|; ratio = median_G / min median_I, scenario-cluster bootstrap 2000 seed 7, win = ratio<1 and CI upper<1.
primary_test: 40% measured, noise-free, 3 seeds pooled, on the carved subgrids that ran: GENCO wins (CI rule) on >= ceil(2/3 n) => PASS else FAIL
secondary_tests: (b) the same rule at 40% with 0.5% noise

(c) SIZE-BANDED comparison against the unseen-family grids reused (not re-run) from candidate 9's verdict.json: bands <=1000 buses and >1000 buses, at 40% noise-free, 20%, 40%+noise: win counts of carved vs unseen per band, Fisher exact p (two-sided, descriptive). ALL carved subgrids are <=1000 buses and the only unseen-family grids <=1000 buses are the six SimBench-HV grids (64-120 buses; the seen-family 500/793-bus GOC grids are not unseen). Above 1000 buses ONLY unseen grids exist, so size is only PARTLY controlled: SimBench-HV is 5-10x smaller than the carved subgrids and electrically different (distribution-voltage HV nets), so the <=1000 comparison also confounds size with family type.
(d) descriptive: tier a vs tier b, by parent, 10% and 20%+noise

outcome_mapping_and_post_sentences.PASS (>= 2/3 of carved subgrids win at 4: Freshly carved subgrids of the seen-family parents, which GENCO never trained on, behave like the seen family (GENCO beats the best classical interpolator on X of N at 40%, CI below 1), not like the unseen families (8/17). So candidate 9's seen/unseen gap is a FAMILY-exposure effect (the pretraining families), not grid memorisation; caveats: our carving may differ from GENCO's, size is only partly controlled, all carved subgrids are <=1000 buses, unaudited.
outcome_mapping_and_post_sentences.FAIL (< 2/3 win): Freshly carved subgrids of the seen-family parents do NOT reproduce GENCO's advantage (X of N win at 40%, needed 2/3). The 15/15 on GOC/EPIGRIDS in candidate 9 is therefore specific to the particular grids/subgrids GENCO trained on (memorisation or train-distribution specifics), not a general family effect; or our carved subgrids differ too much from GENCO's (smaller, boundary-injection-heavy, OPF-screened) to count as in-distribution; the data cannot separate these. Unaudited.
